ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approximately 25% high-intensity (white/cream) pixels to 75% low-intensity (dark grey/black) pixels across the visible ventral surface.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Large contiguous black region occupying the central and lower portions of both lobes. High-contrast white patches are localized at the distal tips. The left distal patch contains several discrete dark circular blobs. Sparse white speckling is visible within the central black field.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Narrow V-shaped central depression with a calculated internal angle of approximately 42 degrees and a bounding-box depth occupying roughly 12% of the vertical fluke span.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Highly irregular trailing edge. The left lobe exhibits five distinct macro-serrations (peaks) with pixel amplitudes ranging from 3-8 pixels. The right lobe shows a more jagged, fine-grained serration pattern with higher frequency but lower individual amplitude.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Convex trajectory along the outer lateral margins, sweeping upward and outward toward the distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: High-density clusters of irregular brownish-grey pixel masses (barnacles) at the extreme tips of both lobes. Multiple small, bright-white circular clusters are scattered across the dark central pigmented areas.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Extensive network of light-colored, unaligned linear pixel disruptions (rake marks) crossing the dark field of both lobes, primarily oriented in diagonal and horizontal vectors.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Prominent barnacle colonization on both distal tips. Extensive linear scarring (rake marks) across the ventral surface. Significant irregular notch on the upper trailing edge of the left lobe.
other_distinctive_markers: A singular, large dark circular pixel cluster (focal spot) isolated within the white pigmentation of the upper-left distal lobe.
